criteria.text: `src/ui/marks.ts` exists, exports `frame` and `axis` (and `overflowList`), imports only `./format.js`, and contains no reference to `document` (`grep -c '\bdocument\b' src/ui/marks.ts` is 0) — checkable the same way `test/atlas-modules-acceptance.test.ts`'s existing DOM-free list works today; that list (`layout.ts`, `format.ts`, `state.ts`, `perf.ts`, `api.ts`) must include `marks.ts`.

`test/atlas-modules-acceptance.test.ts`'s `expected` import-graph dict gains `'marks.ts': ['./format.js']` and `'render.ts'` gains `'./marks.js'` in its own entry; `pnpm test` fails without both edits (delete either one locally and confirm the existing `AC2: the import graph is acyclic…` test goes red, then restore).

Every template literal `marks.ts` builds and hands to a caller for `innerHTML`/`insertAdjacentHTML` is produced with `format.ts`'s `html` tag, not a bare backtick — covered by the existing scan in `test/atlas-modules-acceptance.test.ts` ("no module but format.ts calls esc()", "every template literal that looks like markup is tagged html"), which already walks every file under `src/ui` and therefore needs no new criterion, only `marks.ts` to exist and be picked up by `jsFiles()`.

For every existing `render.test.ts` assertion that matches a substring of painter output (frame attributes, axis line/tick markup, overflow list copy, word mark attributes), the assertion still passes unmodified after the refactor — i.e. no test in `test/render.test.ts` changes its expected strings, only (if at all) its setup. This is `pnpm test` passing with a `git diff` on `test/render.test.ts` touching no `assert.match`/`assert.equal` expected value tied to markup shape.

`paintRuler`, `paintRisingRuler`, `paintTermStrip`, `paintStrip`, `drawMap`, `paintWeek` and every `paint*Loading`/`paint*Error` function keep their existing exported names and return shapes — reuse the issue #151 acceptance style: `paintRuler`'s test ("keeps its own exported shape after the shared paintRulerBody extraction") stays green with no edits, and an equivalent check exists (new or reused) that `paintWeek` and `paintTermStrip` still return/paint what they did before.

`paintAtlasLoading`, `paintTestimonyLoading`, `paintCompareLoading`, `paintRisingLoading` and `paintWeekLoading` build their `<svg>` frame and axis (where they have one) by calling the same `frame`/`axis` functions from `marks.ts` that their live counterpart calls with `ghost: true`/`ghost: false` — checkable by grepping `render.ts` for the ghost painters' bodies and confirming they call `frame(`/`axis(` rather than writing a literal `<svg` or `<line class="…-axis"` themselves; the existing "loading ghosts hold each figure's silhouette, with no invented words" tests in `render.test.ts` keep passing unmodified (criterion 4 covers this already; named here because it is the issue's stated risk).

`render.ts` contains no more than one literal `<svg` string per figure family (atlas/strip/ruler/week) and no literal `<line class="…-axis"` anywhere — grep-checkable: `grep -c '<svg' src/ui/render.ts` drops from its pre-refactor count, and `grep -c 'axis"' src/ui/render.ts` (the class-attribute literal, not calls into `marks.ts`) is 0 outside `marks.ts` itself.
`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` all exit 0, and `public/bundle.js` is regenerated and committed — `test/bundle-freshness.test.ts` passing is the check.

`CLAUDE.md`'s Layout section names `marks.ts`, states it sits between `layout.ts` and `render.ts` in the import order and is DOM-free, and names which pieces it owns (frame, axis, overflow list, and word mark if step 2 landed) — a fact check against `CLAUDE.md`'s prose, not a line-count or heading-position check.

No route, response shape, SQL statement or `seed.json`/fixture entry changes: `git diff` touches only `src/ui/marks.ts`, `src/ui/render.ts`, `test/atlas-modules-acceptance.test.ts`, `test/render.test.ts` (and/or a new `test/marks.test.ts`), `public/bundle.js` and `CLAUDE.md`. `src/server.ts`, `src/graph.ts`, `src/extract.ts`, `src/query.ts`, `test/fixture.ts` and `public/design-5.html` are untouched.
